after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=2\sqrt{{x}^{7}}-{x}^{2}$ at the point $(1,1).$
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2\sqrt{{x}^{7}}-{x}^{2}.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\sqrt{{x}^{7}}-{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{7/2}-{x}^{2}) \\  & =7{x}^{5/2}-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(1)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1)=7(1)^{5/2}-2(1)=5\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=5$ and the coordinates of our point $(1,1),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =5(x-1) \\ y & =5x-5+1 \\ y & =5x-4.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y=5{x}^{2}-7$ at the point $(3,38)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=5{x}^{2}-7.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{2}-7)=10x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(3)=10(3)=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(38) & =30(x-3) \\ y & =30x-90+38 \\ y & =30x-52.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =30x-52 \\ x & =\frac{26}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(\frac{26}{15},0).$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $f(x)=7{x}^{2}-2$ at the point $(2,26)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=7{x}^{2}-2.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{2}-2)=14x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2)=14(2)=28.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(26) & =28(x-2) \\ y & =28x-56+26 \\ y & =28x-30.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $y$-axis, we set $x=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =28(0)-30 \\ y & =-30\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $(0,-30).$

content.problem: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve  $y=2{x}^{2}+8x$ at the point $(2,24).$
content.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+8x.$ Computing the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+8x)=4x+8.\end{aligned}
$$

We then compute ${f}^{′}(2)$, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2)=4(2)+8=16\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=16$ and the coordinates of our point $(2,24),$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(24) & =16(x-2) \\ y & =16x-32+24 \\ y & =16x-8.\end{aligned}
$$
